SMTO-CFG-0050 — SMTO can't start because its schedule check interval is too low

GUID: 5ff1f596-7b37-4db4-a3b0-15a445f8fa9f
Slug: config-agent-events-poll-seconds-must-be-greater
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the time it waits between checks for Schedules that are due is set to zero or less. Your conversations, Schedules and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find where SMTO is started (the terminal command, a startup script or the service settings) and look for a setting named AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_POLL_SECONDS. SMTO takes its Schedule check interval only from that startup setting.
  2. Delete that setting to use the usual 10 seconds, or change it to a positive number of seconds, such as 10. SMTO waits this long between checks, and a wait of zero or less can't work.
  3. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. The interval is read only when SMTO starts.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your Schedules run at their set times.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO, along with the value you set. Don't change other settings that start with AOR_ to clear this error; they control different things.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected agent_events_poll_seconds (environment variable AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_POLL_SECONDS) because it is zero or negative.

What this means

  • agent_events_poll_seconds is zero or negative during application settings validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • agent_events_poll_seconds is zero or negative during application settings validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the event polling interval separately from event execution timeouts.

How to fix it

  • Unset AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_POLL_SECONDS or set it to a positive number of seconds (default 10) in the Server's launch environment, then restart. It sets only the AgentEventScheduler tick interval; event execution timeouts and run history are separate settings.
  • Set agent_events_poll_seconds to the intended positive polling interval.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive polling interval validates.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
